steps.content: Beyond the borders of DisCity, howling gales tear across the landscape, carrying stinging clouds of sand and gravel. The air itself is thick with Mania, an unsettling aura that heralds the approaching Tide of Ashes.
Despite these brutal conditions, your group pilots a sand ship through the storm, struggling toward coordinates that flicker intermittently on your terminal.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: The Tide of Ashes is projected to reach us in 36 hours. We've been en route for five, and the target signal is still elusive.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: At our current rate of advance, completing the rescue within the safety window is statistically improbable.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Chief, given your physical state, are you certain you wish to continue the mission?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm fine... cough cough.
A sharp pain lances through your chest, but you bite it back, managing a terse nod for Siglinde.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The rescue mission is our top priority. We're seeing this through.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: ...I see.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Then I must strongly recommend we increase our pace. To hesitate now is to cede every tactical advantage.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: We're pushing as hard as we can without breaking our necks. We don't need a reminder.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Look around. Visibility's shot to hell. One misstep in this soup, and we're done.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: My apologies. I was speaking from the operational standards of DisCorps.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: It was inconsiderate of me. I should better account for my new team's practical constraints.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: ...What's that supposed to mean?

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: If our "constraints" are such a problem, maybe you should go back to your Nirvana Port! No one's stopping you!
Your voice cuts through the argument, sharp and final.
A heavy silence instantly blankets the sand ship's cabin, thick and abrasive as swallowed grit.

In the sudden void of speech, the rattle of sand against the hull becomes deafening. Siglinde's face is an unreadable mask as she lowers her gaze, while the FAC soldiers instinctively avert their eyes. The atmosphere stretches taut, a bowstring drawn to its limit.
This mission was born from a desperate plea: a distress signal from a border village, soon to be consumed by the advancing Tide of Ashes. You led an FAC squad here without hesitation.

The brutal sandstorms scrambled the signal, rendering the coordinates a ghost on your terminal. That's why Siglinde is here—a senior liaison officer from DisCorps, now with the Bureau. Her expertise was meant to be the key to navigating the storm.
On paper, it was a sound strategy. In reality, you underestimated the deep-seated tension between the FAC and DisCorps.
Throughout the journey, the FAC soldiers have barely concealed their suspicion of the DisCorps liaison, and Siglinde's impeccably professional words have carried subtle, precise barbs in return.
—This can't continue. The team will shatter long before you complete the mission.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I think we're all aware of our current situation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Siglinde is right about the Tide. Speed is critical.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But the FAC's concern is also valid. The worse the conditions get, the more we need caution. A single misstep could doom this entire operation.
Your gaze sweeps the cabin, calm yet resolute, silencing the last of the tension with its unyielding finality.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, the conditions are harsh, but we've faced worse and prevailed. I have no doubt we can do it again. But there's one condition: we act as one.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: On this mission, every single skill set here is indispensable. Our success depends on synergy.
You take a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So I need you all to table the distrust. The mission comes first.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whatever your past affiliations, right now, we are comrades. And comrades trust each other enough to watch their backs.
Your words still carry undeniable weight. The arguing parties fall silent, the tension broken. Seizing the moment, the FAC squad captain steps forward.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: ...Understood, Chief. My apologies.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: I'll ensure my team maintains professionalism. We will coordinate with Liaison Officer Siglinde to complete the mission.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: ...You are the commanding officer of this operation, Chief ${PlayerName}. I will follow your orders.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good. Now let's keep moving.
[Scene Change]
After hours of searching, you finally reach the source of the distress signal. But the sight that greets you steals the very breath from your lungs.

Beneath the ochre haze of the sandstorm awaits the skeletons of a village. Homes are shattered into splinters and rubble. Scattered possessions lie half-buried, telling a silent story of panic and flight. Among the ruins, there is only the wind; not a single soul remains.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: The sandstorm's getting worse, and comms are completely down. Chief, searching the WhiteSands blind isn't just impossible; it's a death sentence...

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Did we... get here too late?

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: No.
Suddenly, a shard of static shatters the grim silence.
You turn to see Siglinde's head bowed over her portable cassette device, her fingers turning the knobs with focused intensity. A moment later, she meets your gaze and gives a sharp, definitive nod.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: I'm picking up a new signal. Faint, but traceable.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: It's constantly moving, though. Survivors must be carrying a portable transmitter as they flee.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: We can follow it, but for precise tracking, we'll need to leave the sand ship and proceed on foot. I've already charted a potential route.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: In a successful rescue? I'm not a professional search-and-rescue dog, Chief. I can't give you odds.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: But as long as that transmitter is active, I can intercept its signal.
She puts it lightly, but her tone leaves no room for debate.
Yet, you feel the fragile calm shatter. A new, more volatile tension grips the air.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier A
steps.content: Leave the sand ship? That's suicide...

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier B
steps.content: With interference this severe from the sandstorm, our top-shelf gear is fried. How is her... cassette player... even getting a signal?
The soldiers whisper among themselves. Some check their own devices, as if to refute her. Others stare with distrust, hard and unmoving, at the equipment in her hands.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier C
steps.content: Can she even guarantee those coordinates? One wrong reading, and we're not just failing a mission; we're getting a burial in the dunes...

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier D
steps.content: What if this is intentional? We've heard the stories about DisCorps. Radicals. War-crazed. Who knows what her real orders are?

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier D
steps.content: I... I don't trust her.
Skeptical murmurs ripple through the ranks, each one tightening the invisible screw of tension. The unease is contagious, spreading faster than any order you could give.
Siglinde offers no justification. She merely lifts her head, her gaze calmly sweeping over the whispering faces. Her expression is a placid lake, her tone as steady and unyielding as stone.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: If you lack confidence in my judgment, you are welcome to wait here. The sandstorm will soon resolve our dilemma.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: No signal means no survivors to rescue anymore. A tragically simple conclusion, isn't it?
She pauses, the corners of her mouth lifting into a smile so impeccably polite it feels more ruthless than the sandstorm screaming outside.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: The storm is dangerous, of course. Prudence is a virtue. But if you're too frightened to even leave the vehicle... perhaps you should reconsider your line of work. "Died Hiding" makes for a poor epitaph.
The words are barely out of her mouth when chaos erupts.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier A
steps.content: Who the hell do you think you are?!

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier B
steps.content: We're not cowards! We're just discussing viable routes. No one's asking for your judgment!

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier C
steps.content: Who made you the commander? You don't get to boss around!

Soldiers surge to their feet, their shouts tangling into a raw chorus of anger. The air crackles as one takes a threatening step forward, then another, escalating in a heartbeat from protest to the brink of violence.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Silence!
A sharp bark from the FAC captain cuts through the uproar before you can even draw breath.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Is this the time for petty infighting? Remember your duty!

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: While our people are waiting for rescue, you'd rather bicker and second-guess here, forget the Chief's words and disgrace the uniform?
His face darkens, a silent promise of reprimand as his gaze sweeps over the men. The soldiers instantly fall into a chastened silence, their heads bowing under the weight of his stare.
Only once the order is restored does he turn to you, his salute crisp and definitive.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Chief, permission to lead a team with Liaison Officer Siglinde to locate the signal source.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: I do. And I accept them.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: I can't verify her intel. But you were right, Chief. The mission comes first.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: If there's even a chance, we have to take it.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Protecting our city-state and its people... that's the duty we swore to uphold. With our lives, if necessary.
Then, without a moment's pause, he fixes his attention on Siglinde.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Can you guarantee that the cassette device won't fail? Even under such heavy electromagnetic interference?
A faint, mocking smile touches Siglinde's lips as she arches a single eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: I assure you, Captain, my "cassette device" is far more reliable than your sanctioned hardware. If you prefer to navigate blind, by all means, proceed without it.
Her retort is a scalpel, precise and sharp. The barb lands perfectly, forcing the FAC captain to draw a slow, measured breath as he visibly masters his temper.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: One more question. Your planned route isn't the most direct path. Are these detours necessary, or a miscalculation?
Siglinde offers a soft, derisive laugh, the kind reserved for the most absurd of jokes.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Ah. So it's my judgment you question.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: This "detour" avoids two Mania concentrations and an unstable sinkhole. Threats that no scanner would be able to register.
She never wavers, her gaze holding a steady, unshakable certainty. Then, abruptly, the edge in her voice melts away.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Believe me, I have no vested interest in your demise. Your mission's success is the only reason I'm here.

Her words linger, a charged silence following them. The team shares a series of uneasy glances. Some wear their skepticism plainly but hold their tongues; others find sudden, furtive purpose in their equipment, their movements now hesitant and cautious.
For a moment, the scene is a tableau of held breaths and suspended action, frozen by tension. And then you step into the center, shattering the stalemate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm going with you.
The FAC captain stares, stunned. The idea that you would join the mission personally had clearly never occurred to him. His shock lasts only a second before it is eclipsed by a flash of deep concern.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Chief, with all due respect, your condition—

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My condition doesn't absolve me of my duty as the MBCC Chief. Mania is my responsibility, same as you.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: ...Understood.
With a solemn expression, the captain turns back to face his team.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: All right, listen up!

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: This bickering ends now. You will set aside your personal grievances. And you will not hold any baseless suspicion.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: As the Chief said, whatever our past affiliations, right now, we are comrades. We move as one, we fight as one. Do I make myself clear?
The FAC soldiers snap their acknowledgment in resolute unison, their voices loud and firm.
Through it all, Siglinde has been a silent observer, her expression unreadable, the same composed and inscrutable smile gracing her lips. You turn, meeting her gaze.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I have complete faith in your expertise. DisCorps wouldn't have sent you if you weren't the best.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Lead us to the villagers. Get us through this before the Tide hits.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whatever our pasts, we share one objective now. What do you say, Siglinde?
At your words, Siglinde offers a graceful, immediate nod.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: I will spare no effort in this mission.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good. Let's move out.
